summary: Feed s122_double is degraded: 72.9% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS 60% tolerance and 4.3% of frames exceed IDS 1518-byte MTU and are dropped. IDS requires full payload, so coverage is reduced on both fronts.

findings.root_cause: Traffic mix upstream is encryption-heavy (TLS/QUIC) with 72.9% of bytes encrypted. No decryption is performed before the packet broker forwards to the IDS, so the IDS only sees ciphertext.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot inspect payloads or apply signatures to encrypted bytes; with 73% encrypted vs 60% tolerance, detection is blind to the majority of traffic and misses malware/C2/exfiltration inside TLS.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext for full-payload inspection. Provide a decrypted copy via a central SSL visibility appliance or selective decryption policy before the IDS, or route high-encryption flows to a tool with decryption capability.

findings.root_cause: Source/aggregation network is sending jumbo frames up to 8058 bytes and the packet broker is forwarding them unchanged to a 1G IDS port limited to 1518 bytes. 91 of 2093 frames (4.3%) exceed the limit.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC drops oversize frames silently, creating a 4.3% visibility gap. Because this IDS needs_full_payload=true, broker-side slicing/trimming to 1518 bytes would also break detection and is not an option.

recommended_fix.why: Frames must fit the IDS MTU without losing payload. Enable jumbo-frame support on the IDS if possible, or adjust broker MTU handling to avoid delivering >1518B frames to this 1G port; do not use slicing due to full-payload requirement.
